subject: Training-freezone tagging and procurement bridge
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@caredyne.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@caredyne.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Training-freezone requirement and tagging — initial ask

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement/legal here at CareDyne asked me to follow up with a few granular items so we can move the DPA/POC forward:

1) We need a firm, contractible "no-training" commitment for tenant interactions classified as sensitive. Can Redwood provide wording that covers live inference and logs (i.e., you will not use or retain these interactions for model improvement)?

2) Operationally: how would we tag traffic so opt-out is enforced end-to-end? We prefer something lightweight (API header or tenant flag) and must understand behavior if a fallback model (e.g., lower-latency variant) does not honor the flag.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: CareDyne has EU and US patients — we need clarity on subprocessor change notifications and any cross-border transfer lanes for data covered by the no-train designation.

4) Evidence: procurement asked for an attestation (quarterly) or a proof artifact showing data flow and that data was not used for training. Is Redwood able to provide a canned evidence pack or escrow option for outputs?

Goal: procurement hopes to finalize commercial terms within three weeks, pending legal language and technical assurances. Can you loop in the right contacts (ops and legal) and propose next steps?

Thanks — happy to set a call if helpful.

— Elena Ortiz
Director, Product & Partnerships
CareDyne Health

Attachment: none

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@caredyne.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Training-freezone requirement and tagging — initial ask

Elena — thanks, and appreciate the clarity on procurement timing. High-level responses below; attaching a short spec (training-freezone-spec-v1.pdf) that describes the APIs and ops guarantees.

1) Contract commitment
We can commit to an explicit, contractible "no training / no model improvement" clause scoped to CareDyne tenant interactions that are flagged as training-freezone. That covers: inference inputs, logs, and ephemeral caches — Redwood will not use flagged material to update any shared or internal model weights. We propose a DPA addendum that references tenant-level flags and the operational enforcement layer.

2) Operational tagging and fallback behavior
- Tagging: we support a tenant-level config and an inline header (X-Redwood-No-Train: true). The header + tenant config is honored at the routing layer and enforced through isolation (requests routed to non-adaptive inference pools or session-scoped ephemeral flows).
- Fallbacks: when a requested model variant is incompatible with non-training enforcement (e.g., a managed adaptive endpoint), our routing policy will: (a) attempt a compatible variant; (b) if none available, return a 409 with a machine-readable reason code to the caller; (c) optionally we can configure an automatic failover to a sanctioned lower-capability model that preserves the no-training constraint. We'll include behavior matrices in the spec.

3) Subprocessors & transfers
We publish a subprocessor list and can provide onshore/EU-only processing lanes (KMS and compute residency) for flagged traffic. Subprocessor additions will be covered under our standard 30-day notice and an escalation path for urgent blocklisting requests. Cross-border flows for training-freezone data are blocked unless explicitly approved in the DPA.

4) Evidence & escrow
We offer an evidence pack: routing logs (hashes only), ephemeral cache snapshots, and a periodic attestation statement signed by our compliance team. For additional assurance, we can integrate an outputs escrow workflow (store a digest or encrypted copy of outputs with an escrow provider) — this is not standard but we can include it as an add-on in the SOW.

Next steps
- Internal: looping in Stephanie (legal) and Neha (ops) on this thread to draft language and an ops checklist.
- Proposed timeline: we can deliver a redline of the DPA addendum + evidence spec within 5 business days.
- Suggested meeting: Thu 18 Jun 10:00 PT for a 30-min run-through. Is that OK?

I'll attach the spec now; follow-ups from legal and ops will come separately.

Best,

Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachment: training-freezone-spec-v1.pdf

Markus / Elena —
Quick clarifying asks from procurement/legal:

- Can you provide sample contract language (we prefer language we can put directly into an amendment) and a short 1-page attestation template we can include in our security appendix?
- If automatic failover returns a 409, what is the expected client experience? Will our integration engineers receive structured error codes to implement a retry/fallback?
- How do you handle subcontractor migrations (e.g., if a subprocessor in the EU is replaced)? We need to know the maximum notice window (we usually require 30 days) and an SLA for our remediation requests.

If Redwood can share the redline + one-pager attestation by end of day Friday, we'll keep pace with the three-week procurement window. Also please confirm whether the escrow option will require a separate PO.

Thanks — Ben

CareDyne Health

Ben / Elena —
Thanks — I'm Stephanie (Head of Contracts). We're aligned on the ask and have prepared a redline of the DPA addendum (attached: care-dpa-addendum-redlines.docx) plus a 1-page draft attestation template. High-level items included in the redline:

- Contract language: explicit tenant-scoped "No Model Improvement" clause that binds Redwood and covered subprocessors; definition of "flagged interaction" and acceptance criteria for the tagging header.
- Fallback behavior: machine-readable error codes (409.NO_TRAIN_COMPAT) and an integration guide; suggested client behavior is to surface a friendly retry option or route to an approved nonadaptive model.
- Subprocessor migrations: 30-day notice by default; expedited 5-day escalation for security/regulatory blocks with an option for temporary suspension of the subprocessor for impacted tenants.
- Evidence cadence: quarterly attestation (signed) + on-demand logs export under NDA; escrow of outputs is available as a billable add-on (separate PO).

Ops note for Neha: please confirm the onshore KMS configuration lead time and whether we can commit to EU-only compute for flagged tenants within the proposed timeline.

Proposed next steps:
1) Mark up the attached redline with any CareDyne edits and return by EOD Fri.
2) Ops sync (technical run-through) — 30 minutes; we suggested Thu 18 Jun 10:00 PT (Markus proposed) but we can flex.
3) Procurement to confirm whether escrow will be on the same PO or separate add-on; Redwood can accommodate either.

Elena / Ben — happy to hop on a call with your counsel.

Regards,
